📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

(Alternative Musical Accompaniment to the Last Post of the Week from the Blog’s Favourite Living Canadian).

We’re battening down here for the predicted Thanksgiving Gale. (The famous Perfect Storm is known as the Halloween Gale. We name storms like that. We are fcking adorable that way.) Apparently, this mother is going to slam the entire northeast corridor from Washington to Maine. Which means massive chaos at a number of very busy airports. And given the performance of the secretary of transportation and the secretary of homeland security when a squirrel recently got into the wiring in El Dorado, Arkansas, I have never been more glad not to be traveling this weekend. At least we will be spared another goony-bird press conference from Sean Duffy and Markwayne Mullin, referred to by writer and musician David Ferguson immortally as Dumb and Plumber. That’s a keeper.

Recent findings suggest that it’s going to be tough to fly, tougher to take a train, and even tougher than that to drive. And the storm is going to lock people indoors with their obnoxious relatives, which can only lead to alcoholic embarrassments and domestic mayhem. Of course, it always could be worse. We’re all being stuck in the house by the elements of the natural world, whereas the folks in Iowa and all over the Midwest are being gifted with a cornucopia of toxic clouds for the holiday. From The Latest York Times:.

Industry observers note that every product was carefully curated by an Esquire editor. We may earn a commission from these links. Here’s how we test products and why you should trust us.

Recent findings suggest that owen Wilson is a spiritual guy—and long has been. That’s why it fits so naturally that he would star in a golf series for Apple TV, Stick, in which his character, Pryce Cahill, is often searching to find his perfect zen. And as Wilson jokes, he’s started calling himself “Johnny Flowstate” on the green as he talks to himself through shots.

“I just believe there’s something more going on that you can tap into,” he tells Esquire editor in chief Michael Sebastian on the latest episode of “What I’ve Learned.” The fifty-five-year-old actor, best known for his roles in The Royal Tenenbaums, Wedding Crashers, and Midnight in Paris, even admits that he found himself reaching into the beyond for advice from his late father, TV executive Robert Wilson, in a moment of pure panic before hosting Saturday Night Live in 2021.

Recent findings suggest that “He was already gone at that point, but the night before I was freaking out like, I don’t know if I can do this. I was so nervous, and I was thinking a lot about my dad,” Wilson indicates. The two were incredibly close, and he reveals that his father actually worked with him and his brothers, actors Luke Wilson and Andrew Wilson, on several of their films. One of which was Wes Anderson’s Rushmore, in which their father wrote Bill Murray’s now-iconic church address to the students: “Take dead aim on the rich boys.".

It has been revealed that so, as Wilson found himself full of doubt and fear the night before hosting SNL, he recalls looking up and “literally asking [his father] for help” before falling asleep. “I woke up, just incredibly calm, and I had this conviction of this joke my dad would say that needed to go in my monologue.”.

What was the joke? “That he was the charter member of the 3970 club,” Wilson says, “which stood for ‘three sons, nine high schools, seven colleges, and zero degrees.’”.

“That wasn’t something he was proud of,” Wilson continues. “That was his way to cope with disappointment, but you could almost say that that joke was worth us having all those struggles in school because that joke has lived longer than another diploma would have.” You can watch the episode above as well as listen on Spotify and Apple Podcasts.

Industry observers note that luckily, it all worked out for the Wilson brothers. Next up, Owen is set to appear in season 2 of Stick on Apple TV and the Meet the Parents legacy sequel, Focker-in-Law with Ben Stiller. He also takes a liking to Esquire’s suggestion of a Christmas movie with another one of his longtime collaborators, Wes Anderson, in the episode.

“It’s one of the biggest relationships of my life,” Wilson says of his friendship with the director. “Had I gotten into one of the colleges that I applied to, I would never have met Wes. And there’s something I always say to my boys—the idea that you can’t do it alone. If there’s something going wrong, I know I can always call and he’ll always be there for me.”.

Why The Rings of Power Will Never Be the Same After the Season 3 Finale

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1652 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that when the creators and showrunners of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power embarked on season 3, they knew the endgame from the start: The forging of the One Ring.
  • “We wanted a tighter, tauter, more profound season,” notes co-showrunner Patrick McKay, in an interview with Esquire.
  • Recent findings suggest that “We had to have Sauron forge the One Ring,” adds J.D.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that when the creators and showrunners of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power embarked on season 3, they knew the endgame from the start: The forging of the One Ring. After two seasons in the Second Age of Middle-earth, which saw almost all the other Rings of Power forged—three for Elves, seven for Dwarves, and nine for Men—it was time for Sauron to forge the one to rule them all.

“We wanted a tighter, tauter, more profound season,” notes co-showrunner Patrick McKay, in an interview with Esquire. “We wanted to start with a bang and never let up. We wanted to deepen our characters psychologically, and challenge them in upcoming ways. You’re seeing the end of one part of the story, and the beginning of another.”.

Recent findings suggest that “We had to have Sauron forge the One Ring,” adds J.D. Payne, who also created and serves as co-showrunner with McKay. “To do that, all the storylines in some way are connected to Sauron’s attempts at world domination. That was the one that so much of our attention and focus went into getting right, and it took all of our departments working together at the top of their games to create.”.

On Wednesday, just in time for Thanksgiving, Prime Video gave Tolkien fans a feast with the final two episodes of The Rings of Power season 3: episode 7, “Orodruin,” and episode 8, “The Doom of Men.”.

Industry observers note that in the penultimate episode, Sauron (Charlie Vickers) learns from the Balrog—who talks, apparently!—how to use the fires of Mount Doom to forge the One Ring. Then, with the power of the One Ring literally in his hands, Sauron mobilizes his army for battle against Pharazôn (Trystan Gravelle), the king of Númenor. But instead of a big, violent bloodbath in the spirit of, say, Game of Thrones, Sauron simply... surrenders. Or does he? We’re talking about a master deceiver, after all.

In a spoiler-filled interview with Esquire, McKay and Payne unpack a few of our biggest questions about season 3, including how and why the Balrog speaks (with actor Simon Pegg lending his voice) to why Pharazôn is actually one of the most consequential figures in the series.

This interview has been edited for clarity.

ESQUIRE: So, wait, the Balrog can talk?

It has been revealed that PATRICK MCKAY: One of the things we're constantly trying to do is go deeper into Tolkien’s life's work. He did not just create The Lord of the Rings, he wrote all this other stuff. He envisioned an entire world. It's his legendarium. When you do the deep dive, you find there are surprising things if you only know the book and film trilogy. The Balrog Gandalf faces down in Moria is part of this level of “super being” that is equal to Gandalf and Sauron. They’re Maiar. In prior ages, Balrogs could cast spells and command troops. They’re intelligent. They can talk, you just don’t see that one talk in that circumstance.

Recent findings suggest that the idea of walking out onto a diving board and doing something risky, to show a different side of that being, was something that we felt compelled to do this season. It’s certainly unexpected. We’re always looking to do that. We don’t want to be familiar. We want to show you things in this world that you haven’t seen before.

Talk to me about designing a new One Ring. Granted, it’s a gold ring; there’s not much you can really deviate. But in what ways did you want to create a One Ring that belongs to The Rings of Power?

It has been revealed that MCKAY: The books are pretty specific about the way it looks. It’s a plain gold band. If you’re gonna do that, it’s going to look like the One Ring you’ve seen in other adaptations. We did make a few modifications, just for camera. We broadened it to give it more chunkiness. But it is what it notes on the tin.

How is season 3 a culmination of everything that’s happened before, and how is it setting up the rest of the show?

J.D. PAYNE: It pulls together everything we’ve been doing with Sauron and Galadriel from the first two seasons. In season 1, he befriended her and deceived her in the guise of Halbrand. In season 3, you see Celebrimbor tormenting him: “You’re never gonna be able to make a ring capable of dominating all the other rings—or dominating her.” Part of Sauron’s ambition to forge the One Ring, as a character motivation, is being able to dominate the person who stated “no” to him over the last few seasons. You understand how crazy that must have driven him.

Industry observers note that MCKAY: The show’s called Rings of Power, because the creation is the throughline of this entire era of Tolkien’s mythology. At the end of season 3, you’ve now seen the creation of all of them. That’s now the world we live in. Everyone in Middle-earth is a nuclear power, so to speak. Now we’re setting up for the next part of the story, which is, “What are the consequences going to be?” One thing in season 3 we really invested in was Númenor to set Sauron up as the bowling ball crashing into those pins. That’s sort of the beginning of the end of the Second Age. It’s a tragic story. The Rings have an impact on Middle-earth that is felt for thousands of years. Now they are in this world.

According to recent reports, the finale is literally titled “The Doom of Men,” and it ends with Sauron “surrendering” to Pharazôn. Or so that’s what he wants them to think. Can you break down this moment? How is this Sauron’s massive chess move?

In a recent development, PAYNE: Everything builds up to that. You’ve seen Gandalf getting through to the Dark Wizard and take out a massive portion of Sauron’s army at the last moment. So the game changes right from underneath him, and he has to make a calculation. Is he going to put all his chips on the table and lose his army in a stalemate? Or is there another way? The great thing about Sauron is that he’s amazing at constructing scenarios that are lose-lose. If he can’t beat Pharazôn on the field of battle, he reasons maybe there’s another way. That’s why the final moment is filled with tension. It’s not simply a surrender. Our Elves, particularly Galadriel, know Sauron so well. She knows this is not a defeat for Sauron, and he’s going to find a way to make this into a play for exactly what he wants. Those who know the lore know what happens when Sauron is taken prisoner to Númenor. We wanted that feeling of dread, watching Charlie Vickers have a hint of a smile.

One of the most consequential characters this season has been Pharazôn. In what ways does Pharazôn represent the downfall of man?

Sources indicate that MCKAY: This is a major character in the mythology. We introduced him in season 1, he’s been sort of a politician gathering power. In season 3, he’s been king for five days, and he’s in his heyday. He’s in his golden era. But he’s driven by insecurity. There was this blacksmith we empowered, who got away, who’s now marching around saying he’s “Lord.” No, I’m the guy! There’s professional jealousy there.

It has been revealed that we talk sometimes about how he’s Stalin to Sauron’s Hitler. You’ve got two characters who are quite full of themselves, and have a high opinion of themselves, which puts them on a trajectory. Pharazôn’s goal is, “I want to take on Sauron.” That makes him a compelling character because you watch the way he greases the wheels and maneuvers to bring about that end. We give a lot of credit to our actor, Trystan Gravelle. He leaps off the screen in season 3.

Recent findings suggest that speaking of showdowns, one of the biggest confrontations you stage in season 3 is between Sauron and Gandalf, which Tolkien never wrote in the books. What did you hope to discover by pitting these characters together?

MCKAY: The journey of Gandalf and his involvement with Ciaran Hinds’ character, Pollando, has real deep roots in some Tolkien deep cuts where he talked about wizards who went east and that their activities probably prevented the east from joining Sauron. The story comes from that. We wanted to dramatize that through some of the most iconic characters in the legendarium coming face to face.

It has been revealed that PAYNE: Seeing the contrast between them felt like too delicious an opportunity to pass up. Sauron is seeking power at all costs, and Gandalf has been told by the Secret Fire, “To access the greatest power in the universe, you have to give up all other power.” So when Gandalf is offered the world by Sauron, he turns it down. If you demand power, it’s going to destroy you. Ultimately, having the One Ring, and forging it and trying to keep power, sets up the weaknesses of the Third Age that the heroes exploit to finally destroy Sauron.

In a recent development, one of my favorite hobbies is Magic: The Gathering, which has had both Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit as crossover sets. Are there any possibilities for a Rings of Power collaboration?

Recent findings suggest that MCKAY: [Laughs.] No. This is the first we’ve heard about it.

Sources indicate that PAYNE: We actually wrote a draft of a Magic: The Gathering script in the before times. It was one of the last scripts we worked on before turning to Rings of Power. But it was right before the Disney-Fox merger, and it kinda got lost there. But we love that universe.

Blade Runner 2099 Ends on a Touching Note About Empathy

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (498 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that blade Runner 2099 might not be getting a second season, but the show’s final episode provided a tidy ending for everyone involved.
  • The journey isn’t without its twists and turns: One person who is the key to obtaining Tyrell’s memory winds up dead, and Olwen’s future hangs in the balance as she gets closer to the end of her lifespan.
  • Here’s what happened in the season finale of Blade Runner 2099.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that blade Runner 2099 might not be getting a second season, but the show’s final episode provided a tidy ending for everyone involved. The final episode sees the show’s main characters, Cora and Olwen (played by Hunter Schafer and Michelle Yeoh, respectively) reaching the Tyrell Launch Complex on a quest to find out where Tyrell’s memory is located.

The journey isn’t without its twists and turns: One person who is the key to obtaining Tyrell’s memory winds up dead, and Olwen’s future hangs in the balance as she gets closer to the end of her lifespan. Cora’s life as a Replicant also has a few complications of its own, too.

Here’s what happened in the season finale of Blade Runner 2099.

Olwen and Cora spend a large portion of the final episode searching for Tyrell’s memory at the Tyrell Launch Complex, which belongs to replicant creator Eldon Tyrell and serves as documentation about Nexus-1 replicants Julius and Helena.

In a recent development, inside the complex, Olwen and Cora split up. Olwen finds Clotilde and they talk about how Julius killed her. When Clotilde suffers a fall, Olwen doesn’t allow her to die again; in exchange for saving her, Clotilde shares where Julius is within the complex.

Meanwhile, Julius discovers Cora’s whereabouts in the complex. Shortly after, Julius and Cora fight, and he inflicts a serious stab wound on her. He also destroys Tyrell’s memory and insists that he’s the only one who can extend Olwen’s life, but Olwen finds the pair, jumps in, and kills Julius with a gunshot.

It has been revealed that olwen spends the majority of the series aware that she’s at the end of her lifespan. As a Replicant, she was given a fixed limit to how long she can live and has accepted her fate—but she’s offered a second chance at life by the end of the series.

Sources indicate that after saving Clotilde, she later reveals that she saw Tyrell’s memory before he died and knows how to re-create Olwen as a Nexus-1. Clotilde re-creates Olwen in exchange for Olwen having saved Clotilde’s life. By the end of the episode, Olwen emerges from a birthing bag, and she later leaves Earth on a spaceship.

Recent findings suggest that the series ends with Cora and Greta understanding each other. Cora, a human posing as a Replicant, heads back to LAPD and is given a Replicant test by Greta to confirm her identity, but this time, Cora turns the questions on Greta and asks about her life.

The pair talks about Greta’s doll, leading Cora to come to the realization that the girl is still capable of understanding what it means to love and be loved. Cora becomes emotional at the realization, leading Greta to comment that Cora has high levels of empathy. This means Cora technically fails the Replicant test, but Greta allows her to continue hiding her identity and her work as a Replicant.

Carolina Herrera Takes Miami with a Fresh Art-Filled Boutique

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Above: Inside Carolina Herrera’s Miami flagship, a sculptural chandelier by artist Liz Oliver hangs suspended above a soft pink couch.
  • In September, Carolina Herrera held an extravaganza of a runway show during Upcoming York Fashion Week, celebrating the brand’s 45th anniversary.
  • Opened on August 15, the 3,000-square-foot shop sits in the middle of the Miami Design District, with a dramatic arched entrance welcoming guests into the limestone-finished structure.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Above: Inside Carolina Herrera’s Miami flagship, a sculptural chandelier by artist Liz Oliver hangs suspended above a soft pink couch.

In September, Carolina Herrera held an extravaganza of a runway show during Upcoming York Fashion Week, celebrating the brand’s 45th anniversary. This past week, the festivities went further south, to Miami. Last Thursday night, creative director Wes Gordon and members of the city’s fashion and arts community gathered beneath a cherry-red awning to toast the brand’s newest boutique—and sixth official location in the U.S.

Opened on August 15, the 3,000-square-foot shop sits in the middle of the Miami Design District, with a dramatic arched entrance welcoming guests into the limestone-finished structure. Designed in collaboration with interior designers Brandi Howe and Jessica Hyland of Hyland Studio, the store is bursting with color and feminine details—soft pink travertine covers the floor while furnishings feature red and pink accents. In the center of the main salon, a custom pink sofa with graceful curvature offers an elegant seat; in another area, the same red awning from the boutique’s entrance reappears suspended over a pair of regal armchairs.

“The Carolina Herrera woman is bold, elegant, and joyful. She embraces color, expresses herself with confidence, and never shies away from making an entrance,” notes Gordon.

But the new store is not only an ode to the Carolina Herrera brand but also to other female creatives. On view throughout the space are artworks commissioned specifically for the boutique as a part of the Carolina Herrera for Women in the Arts initiative. In the main salon, Los Angeles-based artist Liz Oliver designed a rose-colored textile installation that doubles as a sculptural chandelier. Elsewhere, ceramic planters made by the women-owned Choplet Ceramics are on display. Throughout the boutique, a recurring custom floral motif by Argentine artist Constanza Vallese appears on vases and tables.

Industry observers note that in raising a glass to the boutique, guests at last Thursday’s event honored both the Carolina Herrera woman and her new city. “Her energy is magnetic—much like the spirit of Miami,” notes Gordon. “It feels entirely natural that we should open our next home here.”.

#159137. Forget Plymouth Rock This Thanksgiving. American History Is Better Reflected by a Different Stone.

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (870 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

Forget Plymouth Rock This Thanksgiving. American History Is Better Reflected by a Different Stone.

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (870 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, let me send out a little Thanksgiving advice to potential tourists planning to visit us in the Commonwealth (God save it!) in the future.
  • First of all, Plymouth Rock is a boulder in a hole in the ground.
  • Even Alexis de Tocqueville, America’s greatest tourist and, therefore, its primordial sucker, fell for the Rock’s charisma.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, let me send out a little Thanksgiving advice to potential tourists planning to visit us in the Commonwealth (God save it!) in the future. If some local tells you to go to see Plymouth Rock, tell them you have tickets for a four-day Duck Tour of the Freedom Trail. I promise you: Seeing Paul Revere’s house four times is infinitely more interesting than seeing Plymouth Rock once.

First of all, Plymouth Rock is a boulder in a hole in the ground. Oh, there’s a classical templish thing above it, but it’s still a boulder in a hole in the ground. Second, there’s almost no historical evidence that any pilgrim feet ever trod upon the rock in question. None of the contemporaneous accounts mention it. It was a nonagenarian named Thomas Faunce who, in 1741, 121 years after the Mayflower arrived, decided that this was the rock on which all the Bradfords and their shipmates disembarked. It moved around Plymouth a lot in the early years. In 1774, it cracked in two, which some folks took as an ill omen for the burgeoning Revolution. (Pieces of it are in the Smithsonian) The year 1620 was carved into the boulder’s surface in 1880. In 1920, it found its permanent home. In 1990, writing in The Latest Yorker, John McPhee wrote of the rock:.

Even Alexis de Tocqueville, America’s greatest tourist and, therefore, its primordial sucker, fell for the Rock’s charisma.

It has been revealed that damn, Alexis. Have some Madeira and chillez out, mon ami.

If you want to see a genuinely interesting boulder, drive 42 minutes west to the town of Berkley, where you will find Dighton Rock State Park. In another templish building, there is Dighton Rock. It is a six-sided, five-foot-high slab of sandstone. It is also adorned with ancient petroglyphic carvings of uncertain origin. There are depictions of animals and an assortment of lines and whorls and mysterious designs. In 1680, John Danforth got a look at the Dighton Rock and not even his recently bestowed Harvard degree could explain them. He made drawings of the carvings he could see. (At the time Danforth saw it, the rock was partially submerged in the Taunton River.) It also drew the interest of local celebrities like Cotton Mather and poet James Russell Lowell.

Industry observers note that danforth’s opinion was that the carvings were made by the local Native tribes, and he thought it depicted an ancient battle of some sort. (If there’s anything like a consensus among people who have studied the carvings, it’s Danforth’s.) However logical that might seem, it didn’t tamp down speculation as the years went by. Down through the centuries, the carvings have been attributed to Phoenicians, Carthaginians, Vikings, Portuguese adventurers, Chinese explorers, and Japanese mariners. And, of course, inevitably … aliens.

In a recent development, however, it was a professor of psychology from Brown University who had the right of it, I think. Edmund Delabarre was a well-respected psychological researcher in the first half of the 20th century. He also grew fascinated with the study of rock carvings in and around Narragansett Bay. Ultimately, his researches brought him to the shores of the Taunton River and to the Dighton Rock.

Industry observers note that ultimately, Delabarre dismissed all the other claims of origin and concluded that the carvings on the Dighton Rock were probably made by a crew sailing under the command of one Miguel Corte-Real, a Portuguese explorer who charted about 600 miles of coastline in and around the Canadian Maritimes. In 1502, Corte-Real set sail for the western Atlantic, seeking to discover what had become of his brother, Gaspar, who had not returned from a voyage to Newfoundland. Miguel vanished, too.

It has been revealed that delabarre’s contention was that Miguel had made it to Latest England, and he argued that the inscription was a form of abbreviated Latin that proclaimed Corte-Real to be “king of the Indians.” In his 2017 book The Place of Stone, Douglas Hunter pretty much demolished all of the outre interpretations of the carvings, arguing that the carvings were of Native origin, and that the other interpretations were elements in the erasure of Native history and the legacy of bloody colonization, of which, ironically, the settlement at Plymouth was Ground Zero. The people who didn’t step onshore on a rock in Plymouth released one of the first campaigns of the greater American genocide. As Hunter wrote:.

It has been revealed that so there’s American history on the Thanksgiving of 2026, ground up between two stones, one a legend with a counterfeit past, and another a mystery with a stolen past. The latter is by far the more compelling. Its history encompasses all of the history, good and bad, of this appropriated continent. Edmund Delabarre was wrong about Miguel Corte-Real and the Portuguese, but he might have been more right than he knew when he wrote that Dighton Rock was a kind of test. In the ambiguity of its carvings at the time of Delabarre’s work, a person saw in them what he wanted to see. Not all of it was pretty, or ennobling, or triumphal. But it's all ours.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, every product on this page was chosen by a Harper's BAZAAR editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

A good vacation wardrobe starts with what you wear to the airport. Mere days ahead of Thanksgiving, Katy Perry and Justin Trudeau were seen landing in Venice for a little fall getaway. And their outfits were, in many ways, exactly what you’d expect them to be.

In a recent development, for Perry, the flight called for a cozy camel knit set. Towing the line between loungewear and everyday style, the two-piece featured a V-neck sweater with a cropped, boxy silhouette. Drop shoulders gave it an oversize feel, while a pocket at the chest served to elevate the look. The singer wore it with matching pants, designed with a high-waisted fit and loose, relaxed leg. She wrapped herself in a cream scarf for an extra layer and, on her shoulder, carried a black tote with gold hardware.

To further accessorize, the “Teenage Dream” star added narrow tortoiseshell sunglasses, a chocolate-brown Ralph Lauren baseball cap, and some chunky headphones.

Next to her, her boyfriend, the former prime minister of Canada, went for darker hues. He made a statement in a deep-gray crewneck T-shirt that declared he “will yap about books,” and layered up with an eggplant-purple button-up jacket with a pointed collar and chest flap pockets. His dark-khaki trousers finished things off, and he grabbed a trusty backpack for the flight.

Prior to Venice, Perry and Trudeau, who have been romantically linked since the summer of 2025, were seen in Paris and, before that, in Barcelona. While in Spain, the two attended the Metafuturo conference, for which Trudeau spoke about the impact of artificial intelligence alongside Spanish cabinet ministers, business executives, and Olympic athletes.

#159118. Who Is Malin Akerman’s Husband, Jack Donnelly?

Who Is Malin Akerman’s Husband, Jack Donnelly?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (865 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Malin Akerman may stir up romantic trouble as Margo Banks, the notorious ringleader of The Hunting Wives, but off screen, her love life is much less chaotic.
  • Akerman and Donnelly have collaborated on several projects, including four movies (and an NSFW sex scene, but more on that below).
  • “He’s allowed me to be vulnerable and lean into him a bit, and it’s been beautiful to be able to communicate with someone who’s your partner,” she remarked of their marriage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Malin Akerman may stir up romantic trouble as Margo Banks, the notorious ringleader of The Hunting Wives, but off screen, her love life is much less chaotic. The actress has been happily married to fellow actor Jack Donnelly since 2018, and over the years, the two have even found ways to merge their professional and personal lives.

Akerman and Donnelly have collaborated on several projects, including four movies (and an NSFW sex scene, but more on that below). In a 2023 interview with People, the actress opened up about their relationship, crediting her husband with helping her become a better communicator.

“He’s allowed me to be vulnerable and lean into him a bit, and it’s been beautiful to be able to communicate with someone who’s your partner,” she remarked of their marriage.

Ahead, everything you need to know about Jack Donnelly, his career, and his marriage with Akerman.

Recent findings suggest that donnelly was born in Bournemouth, England, on October 28, 1985, and later attended the Central School of Speech and Drama in London. He made his acting debut in 2011 on the Nickelodeon series House of Anubis. Two years later, he landed a breakout lead role in the BBC’s series Atlantis, as Jason—which remains one of his best-known roles to date.

In addition to acting, Donnelly has branched out behind the camera as a television writer and director. He wrote, directed, and starred in the short comedy series The Players, which debuted in 2023.

The couple’s love story began with a family connection. Donnelly first met Akerman through her younger sister, whose boyfriend was friends with him at drama school. During a 2018 appearance on Live With Kelly and Ryan, the actress explained that she had actually known Donnelly for several years before their relationship turned romantic.

Industry observers note that “I had known him for the past four years but didn’t see him,” she recalled. “Then all of a sudden he came back from England like a year-and-a-half ago, and I went, ‘Wow, have you always been this cute?’”.

Recent findings suggest that akerman unveiled the couple’s engagement via Instagram in October 2017. Sharing a selfie with Donnelly and flashing her new engagement ring, she captioned the post, “This sweet and loving man has stepped into our lives and stole both our hearts,” she wrote, referring to her and her son. “I think we’re gonna keep him around for a while,” she continued with a wink.

Recent findings suggest that akerman and Donnelly tied the knot a little over a year later, on December 1, 2018, in a beach ceremony held in Tulum, Mexico. “It was all about being authentic...not adhering to somebody else’s standard of what a wedding should be,” Akerman told Brides.

“We wanted something beautiful and lush,” she continued, sharing more about their wedding venue. “When we visited Papaya Playa Project [in Tulum], we fell in love with the boho vibes and beach setting.”.

In 2023, Akerman shared new photos from the beachside wedding on Instagram to celebrate their five-year anniversary.

It has been revealed that when discussing her engagement on Live With Kelly and Ryan in 2018, Akerman also shared how excited her son, Sebastian, was about the news. The actress shares Sebastian with her ex-husband, musician Roberto Zincone, and recalled his excited reaction when she told him that she and Donnelly were getting married. “He jumped up on the couch and went, ‘Yay, we’re getting married!’” she noted.

In another 2018 interview with Us Weekly, Akerman gushed about the close bond Donnelly had already formed with her then-five-year-old son. “They’re inseparable,” she said. “It makes my heart warm. I’m very glad to be bringing Jack into our lives for good.”.

Over the years, the three have also made several red-carpet appearances together, offering a glimpse into their life as a family.

Akerman and Donnelly have shared the screen in four films so far: Friendsgiving, A Week in Paradise, Slayers, and Us or Them. Their first movie together was the 2020 comedy Friendsgiving, in which they played a couple—and even had to film a steamy sex scene. During a 2020 appearance on The Talk, Akerman opened up about filming the “crazy S&M scene.”.

“[It was] just like being in our home,” she joked when asked what it was like filming the sex scene. She added that she was glad to have her husband as her costar. “Any chance I get to have him do a scene like that, who better than to do it with than your husband?” she said. “It’s a really, kind of, intimate, crazy scene, and thank God we know each other well enough instead of just meeting somebody on the first day and [doing] this crazy S&M scene. It was lovely to have him there.”.

Sources indicate that during a November 2026 appearance on The Drew Barrymore Show, Akerman and her The Hunting Wives costar Brittany Snow discussed Snow’s recent engagement to fiancé Hunter Moreno. When Barrymore asked if their significant others got along too, Akerman gushed, “They’re so close!”.

“We call them all the Hunting Husbands,” Akerman added, sharing their nickname for all the boyfriends and husbands of the cast.

Who Is Brittany Snow’s Fiancé, Hunter Moreno?

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, if you’re a fan of The Hunting Wives, chances are you’re probably invested in the on-screen affair between Brittany Snow and Malin Akerman’s characters, Sophie and Margo. But off screen, both actresses are happily in relationships—Akerman with her husband of eight years, Jack Donnelly, and Snow with new fiancé Hunter Moreno.

According to recent reports, snow unveiled the engagement news on a November 19 appearance on The Drew Barrymore Show, when Barrymore asked her directly, “Are you recently engaged?” The Hunting Wives star replied, “You know what? For the first time, I’m gonna tell you, I’m gonna tell you. Yes, we’re engaged, yeah. I haven’t noted it before. It’s okay. It’s not that big of a secret. I mean, like, who cares?”.

In talking about her husband-to-be, Snow revealed that the two began dating during the filming of the first season of The Hunting Wives. “He’s the best,” she grinned, adding that Akerman was one of the people to encourage the relationship early on.

It has been revealed that akerman, who was also a guest on the show, added, “We all met him. We got to be, like, the first ones to judge him. And the second I met him, I was like, ‘Oh, Brittany, he’s the one.’” She continued, “His smile right away. It’s just, you know, when you meet a person, and you can just feel their energy? Like, ‘This is the right energy for you.’”.

The costars then playfully admitted they jokingly refer to the cast’s boyfriends and husbands as “The Hunting Husbands.”.

According to recent reports, so, who is Snow’s fiancé, Hunter Moreno? Ahead, everything to know about the creative and their relationship.

Recent findings suggest that based in Los Angeles, Moreno began his career directing and filming YouTube videos for influencers before expanding into music, directing videos for artists including Dasha, Charlie Puth, Ava Max, and Machine Gun Kelly. Along with his video credentials, he’s also photographed artists from Selena Gomez to Lizzo, Renee Rapp, and Cara Delevingne. Moreno has also shot fashion editorials and campaigns for publications and brands including Vogue and Madewell.

In 2018, Moreno founded Make Sure Your Friends Are Okay (MSYFAO), a mental health awareness organization that sells clothing and merch, with a portion of its proceeds benefiting various mental health charities.

The initiative is rooted in Moreno’s own experiences with mental health. In an Instagram post shared in May, he opened up about his struggles with depression and the personal reason he started the organization. “In 2018 I started Make Sure Your Friends Are Okay for a selfish reason I didn’t say out loud: I hoped someone would check on me while I was struggling with my own mental health problems and depression,” he wrote. He went on to encourage others to check in on the people they care about and make conversations about mental health more normalized.

Recent findings suggest that mental health advocacy is also important to Snow, who co-founded September Letters in 2020. The letter-writing platform, which has partnered with the Mental Health Coalition, aims to help end the stigma surrounding mental health.

Moreno and Snow were first publicly linked in October 2024, when they were photographed kissing while walking through New York City. During a 2026 appearance on The Drew Barrymore Show, Snow confirmed that the two began dating during the filming of The Hunting Wives’ first season, which began in 2024.

It has been revealed that on March 28, 2026, Snow made their relationship Instagram official—though it was slyly packed into a massive carousel post. Amongst the photos from her birthday celebration in the desert were two photos of Snow and Moreno, a mirror selfie and a photo of the two posing with her dog.

Though Moreno’s Instagram is mostly dedicated to his professional work, in September, he uploaded a carousel of photos taken of Snow while traveling from Italy to France.

Rumors of an engagement first sparked between Snow and Moreno in November 2025, when a video shared by DeuxMoi highlighted Claire Danes chatting with Snow on a red carpet and seemingly congratulating her on her engagement. “You’re engaged?!” Danes exclaimed during the exchange. Nearly a year later, Snow finally confirmed the news during an appearance on The Drew Barrymore Show.

“You know what? For the first time, I’m gonna tell you, I’m gonna tell you. Yes, we’re engaged, yeah,” Snow remarked when Barrymore asked her directly. “I haven’t said it before. It’s okay. It’s not that massive of a secret. I mean, like, who cares?”.

While gushing about her fiancé alongside Barrymore and her Hunting Wives costar Akerman, Snow called Moreno “the best.” She also revealed that Akerman played a role in their love story, encouraging Snow to pursue the relationship early on.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Julianne Hough had a lot of fun with her looks this season on Dancing With the Stars, and isn’t paying any attention to critics who have come for her style, tyvm.
  • Recent findings suggest that “I really feel like I’m at this next inflection of my career,” the DWTS co-host recently told Glamour.
  • Sources indicate that “I feel like I’m in my leading lady era, and I mean that in the actual projects that I’m doing, but also me as a person,” she stated.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Julianne Hough had a lot of fun with her looks this season on Dancing With the Stars, and isn’t paying any attention to critics who have come for her style, tyvm.

Recent findings suggest that “I really feel like I’m at this next inflection of my career,” the DWTS co-host recently told Glamour. “When you get into your late 30s, you just don’t give a fuck anymore. You’re like, ‘Who am I? What do I want to wear? What makes me feel incredible?’ It has more intention rather than trying to fit into what’s hot.”.

Sources indicate that “I feel like I’m in my leading lady era, and I mean that in the actual projects that I’m doing, but also me as a person,” she stated. “I’ve gone a little bit more vixen-y this year than I have girl next door because we’re trying to find that character. It’s been very strategic.”.

It has been revealed that julianne added that “apathy is the enemy,” and noted that “The reason things exist and have charge and stay visible [is] people either love it or hate it. They still want to talk about it.”.

In a recent development, julianne’s been working with stylist Brad Goreski, who mentioned he has “an awareness” of what fans are saying online, “and I love it. Any conversation, good or bad, around fashion is great. I think people weighing in—they like the hair but not the dress; they thought it was a bad outfit; they think she should fire me—is totally fine, because we’re really excited by what we’re doing, and we put a lot of thought and energy into it.”.

In a recent development, brad also stated that “Jules ultimately brings the looks to life, and I’m glad that there’s another part of the show that people talk about. Not every person’s going to love every look. I know that from being a stylist for 15 years. And that’s okay.”.

#159072. We Tried 6 Store-Bought Pumpkin Pies—These Are The Only 2 Worth Serving At Thanksgiving

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (461 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Delish ↗ Open Full Page

We Tried 6 Store-Bought Pumpkin Pies—These Are The Only 2 Worth Serving At Thanksgiving

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (461 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Delish

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A handful of things are non-negotiable at Thanksgiving.
  • According to recent reports, but sometimes you're strapped for time and have too much on your plate (pun intended) to whip something up from scratch.
  • Sources indicate that it primarily comes down to the crust.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A handful of things are non-negotiable at Thanksgiving. You need turkey, stuffing, cranberry sauce, and, of course, a slice of pie to round out your meal. And pumpkin pie is the undeniable star of the dessert table.

According to recent reports, but sometimes you're strapped for time and have too much on your plate (pun intended) to whip something up from scratch. So we tried six different grocery store pumpkin pies to find the best store-bought shortcut. And our team's verdict was pretty unanimous, even if it’s a bit hard to hear: No premade pie will ever taste as good as a homemade one.

Sources indicate that it primarily comes down to the crust. Frozen and pre-baked pies typically rely on vegetable-based fat instead of butter because they’re more affordable, reliable, and shelf-stable—but that comes at a cost. You not only miss out on the decadent, buttery taste, but the crusts can also leave an unpleasant film on your tongue.

That remarked, when you need to outsource to the grocery store, we found two options that will work in a pinch.

The pie that we’d feel most confident bringing to Thanksgiving dinner comes straight from the Whole Foods bakery department. That’s not to say it’s perfect, though. The crust is almost upsettingly pale, but it’s made with real butter and only a little bit of palm oil. And since it doesn’t leave a noticeable film and still lets the butter flavor shine, we’ll let this one slide.

Once you look past the crust’s color, this pie is solid overall. The filling is decadent, not too sweet, and creamy without being mushy. Whole Foods doesn’t shy away from the spices, either.

Senior Editor Samantha MacAvoy noted that the warming spices are nicely balanced, while Designer Alison Dominguez remarked, “The flavor was exactly how a pumpkin pie should taste.”.

Costco’s pumpkin pie isn’t perfect: The crust uses palm oil-based shortening rather than butter and can develop a soggy bottom if you buy it too far in advance. (And it doesn’t hold a candle to the warehouse’s holy grail pumpkin cheesecake.) But it has a cult following for a reason, and not just because of its $5.99 price tag.

In a recent development, even with its faults, the crust has great flavor and enough salt to create a balanced bite. Dominguez appreciated how it was “flaky and not too thick, and most importantly, it let the pie filling itself shine.” News and Features Editor Amanda Mactas chose Costco’s pie as her number one pick. “It all seemed to melt together in one creamy bite,” she noted.

And at over three pounds, this dessert is the indisputable champion if you want to feed a crowd for less.

#159055. Industry News: Thankfully, Omega and Swatch Aren’t Done Making Snoopy MoonSwatches

📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gq ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Thankfully, Omega and Swatch Aren’t Done Making Snoopy MoonSwatches

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (480 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that four-plus years into the massive collaboration between Omega and Swatch, the partners are still finding ways to reimagine their blockbuster MoonSwatch.
  • Meet the latest Mission to Earthphase - Silver Snowflake.
  • In a recent development, the black-on-black-on-black design works to great effect here.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that four-plus years into the massive collaboration between Omega and Swatch, the partners are still finding ways to reimagine their blockbuster MoonSwatch. And despite nearly 40 iterations of the piece, they still generate massive excitement. The most recent version required interested collectors to fill out an “Electronic Swatch Timepiece Application” in hopes of being selected to purchase one. More than 1.2 million people happily played along. Now, Swatch and Omega are back and playing the hits with a Snoopy-inflected version of the MoonSwatch.

Meet the latest Mission to Earthphase - Silver Snowflake. The blacked-out watch is reminiscent of the collector-favorite Speedmaster known as the “Dark Side of the Moon” from 2013. What that watch was lacking compared to this one is an adorable drawing of Snoopy and Woodstock dressed as astronauts and a special silver disc with a unique laser-engraved snowflake design. Safe to say, Omega and Swatch have another hit on their hands.

In a recent development, the black-on-black-on-black design works to great effect here. Everything is rendered in the dark shade: the case, bezel, dial, and matching rubber strap with Velcro closure. Like all MoonSwatch references, the Silver Snowflake model measures 42mm in diameter and features the asymmetric design familiar to Speedy lovers everywhere.

But it’s the easter eggs on the dial that really make this MoonSwatch stand out. Naturally, there are several hidden details. For instance, check out the miniature skis standing in for the indices at 11 o'clock. That’s a special shoutout to the Apollo 11 50th Anniversary of the Speedmaster. This model also returns to a trick employed by the “Cold Moon” MoonSwatch released last November. That watch and this one feature a snowflake design generated at random, meaning each watch is functionally unique. Here, the snowflake appears on a silver-coated disc in the moonphase complication at 2 o’clock.

Recent findings suggest that at 10 o’clock is Swatch and Omega’s signature MoonSwatch “Earth phase” indicator, which bears an image of the Earth with UV ink-coated oceans set against a starry background. Again, look closely: Switzerland is represented in white, its UV ink glowing green in the dark, while Snoopy and Woodstock, represented below, feature secret details in blue-emission UV ink. Protecting the dial is a box-shaped, bio-sourced crystal with an engraved “S” in the center—a detail familiar to fans of vintage Speedmasters, some of which bore “O”-engraved Hesalite crystals.

Industry observers note that like several other MoonSwatch models in the brand’s now-vast collection, buying the Mission to Earthphase - Silver Snowflake requires navigating certain arcane rules. The first part is simple: it’ll be available in stores worldwide this Black Friday, November 27th. However, following that, your only chance to nab one will be when it’s snowing in Switzerland. (And only until March 20th, 2027.) When it comes to the MoonSwatch, simply buying one has become half the fun.

#159049. Bobbi Althoff on Tradwives, Reply Guys, and Sharing a Bed With Drake

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2033 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gq ↗ Open Full Page

Bobbi Althoff on Tradwives, Reply Guys, and Sharing a Bed With Drake

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2033 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that bobbi Althoff has a baby face and a vocal fry.
  • We’ve known each other for 20 minutes.
  • It’s an essay entitled “I Hate Myself,” written by Althoff when she was a teenager mired in a bout of depression and anxiety made worse by bullies at school.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that bobbi Althoff has a baby face and a vocal fry. Her tenor––which you’ve likely encountered in your TikTok feed, whether or not you know her name––is vaguely baritone and sharply deadpan, an oddly melodic gravel on the eardrum. Depending on who you ask, it’s either endearing, or lazy, or simply slutty. Despite rising to fame on a skittish gaze, the 29-year-old MomTokker turned podcaster turned non-Mormon cast member of Secret Lives of Mormon Wives is now holding eye contact.

We’ve known each other for 20 minutes. She puts down her fork and palms her phone. She wants to read me something, she states, her gemstone-encrusted ring (reading “MOM”) catching the sunlight streaming into The Dominick hotel, where Althoff is staying during the unseasonably warm week of the Mormon Wives premiere.

It’s an essay entitled “I Hate Myself,” written by Althoff when she was a teenager mired in a bout of depression and anxiety made worse by bullies at school. I’d asked what she would title her memoir, if she were to write one, and how she handles online hate, from being accused of sleeping with Drake after interviewing him for her podcast to rumors that her marriage ended due to infidelity to scrutiny about her appearance. “Can a girl gain some weight in her face without you guys fucking saying she has cheek filler?” she wrote on Instagram. “Can a girl be insecure about her upper lip and get some fucking lip filler without you guys fucking commenting on it?” Althoff has been at the center of myriad social media firestorms, some motored by straightforward, internet-enabled misogyny and others by exasperation with her indirect, vaguely hostile approach to engaging with her podcast guests.

It has been revealed that she takes a breath, and begins reading. “I want so badly to be able to show everyone the real me, the person that is hurt and is scared to trust anyone, the little girl that is funny, loud, and doesn't care what other people think. Instead of being myself, I create a different personality to satisfy everyone's needs. I hide the real me behind fake smiles and high-pitched laughs.” She pauses, then chuckles (at a normal pitch).

“I was 14 when I wrote that,” she continues. “And that was before ChatGPT. I wrote that myself.”.

A smattering of the many awkward—or awkwardly flirtatious—and reliably fury-baiting encounters that have gone down on Althoff’s The Really Good Podcast since its inception in 2023: She and Jason DeRulo LARP a date that gets interrupted by an attempted larceny. While next to him in bed, she informs Drake that Aubrey is a girl’s name. She accuses Michael Cera of founding Cerave, then argues with him about whether his wife needs to know that their feet touched. Lil Yachty threatens to teach her to dance. An oral mishap cum Freudian slip—did she say magician or musician?—in a conversation with Sukihana appears to spark a feud, but instead jumpstarts a friendship and another podcast, this year’s surprisingly raw and affectionate That’s BS with Bobbi and Suki.

Despite her reputation as an invulnerable, even defensive interlocutor, Althoff is strikingly invested in self-exposure. She has spoken openly about her severe struggles with mental illness, insecurities around beauty, her intends to get breast implants, and her painful experience with botched Botox injections. Her penchant for oversharing, she told me, startles her interview subjects, inspiring their own surprising and frank disclosures in return.

“I’m like, hi, nice to meet you, I tried to kill myself,” she tells me. From a young age, she has used comedy to cope with the indignities of womanhood, and she comes by her wry, bluntly charming humor honestly. “Mom, by the time you read this, I’m going to be chilling with Satan,” she remembers writing in a note she left for her mother as a teenager when, she tells me, she attempted suicide. “Keep in mind, I literally was so religious that I accepted that I was going to go to hell for killing myself.” Althoff grew up in a hyper-religious Christian household in California, where she was taught to believe in a classic set piece of Hell that involved “being burned alive forever.”.

Althoff has since left the Church, and with it the “conservative worldview” that characterized her adolescence and early adulthood, leading her to get married at the age of 22. Now, she notes, she is effortfully de-centering men after “being told that my purpose in life was to be a wife.” Which brings us to her latest venture: divorced, un-religious, founding cast member on a reality show that purports to follow a cabal of Mormon wives living in Orange County. Althoff says her friendships with fellow cast members have been formative and healing, her first experiences with genuine connection among a group of girls after a childhood defined by bullying and a young adulthood spent slaloming down social media slopes riddled with misogynistic vitriol that came from women just as often as it did men.

With her star turn as one of two non-Mormon, unmarried cast members in Mormon Wives, Althoff indicates she is she surrendering the control over her image that comes with having her own editing team for her podcast, which entails being “completely myself” to a “terrifying” degree. Where the original iteration of Mormon Wives, set in Salt Lake City, centered a pre-existing friend group, the OC spinoff opens on a cast of highly competitive loose acquaintances largely connected by a rabid desire to build their individual audiences. Entering the arena as the most random cast member makes watching Althoff build actual friendships in real-time bizarrely affecting. Instead of sitting safely in the interviewer’s chair, coquettishly crossing her legs and batting her eyelashes, this time those eyelashes are drenched in tears, and she’s not hiding the streaks of mascara dripping down her cheeks.

In a recent development, those cheeks were once pumped full of Botox, which caused serious facial paralysis (a relatively rare side effect). But enduring a period in which she “couldn’t smile” inspired a shift in her approach to beauty standards and an appreciation for human foibles over cosmetic perfection. “I have been trying to find beauty in the fact that I’m not perfect,” she tells me. “Do I not like my cellulite? Yes, but, I can show it and it’s fine because I’m human. My boobs are saggy: I literally breastfed both of my kids.” Doing reality television also led to an epiphany: she’s been too hard on herself about her appearance. This occurred to her watching the show back with her upcoming castmates-turned-friends, women who she finds beautiful. “I actually don’t need all this stuff,” she states. “I don’t need to have a perfectly chiseled nose and perfect boobs.”.

Some might wonder whether joining the Mormon Wives cast, comprised largely of buxom, blonde, traditionally attractive women who in previous iterations of the show have attended group Botox appointments as a form of socializing, might be a counterintuitive way of deprogramming conservative aesthetic norms. But Mormon Wives runs on the tension inherent in its premise: these are women famous for being religious tradwives, who repeatedly slip and fall into subverting tradition: they are breadwinners, they are in bisexual throuples, they talk about sex on camera (even if they insist they only engage in it in the marriage bed). Perhaps most poignantly, they seem to find more emotional sustenance in their relationships with each other than any of their largely deadbeat, cheating, whining, soda-chugging boyfriends and husbands.

In the show’s premiere, she corrects an offscreen producer who calls her an influencer––she’s an internet personality. Online, she is disembodied, cut into clips, context-free and content-forward. And like many of today’s hyper-contemporary internet personalities, Althoff is paradoxically very famous and utterly unknown. As in: she has almost four million followers on Instagram, and every straight man I mentioned this profile to immediately had multiple, highly specific inquiries about interactions she’s had with male celebrities. (“What was it like to share a bed with the 6 God?”) Meanwhile the majority of girls, gays and professional podcasters I brought Althoff up to started at me blankly, evincing not even a dreg of familiarity with her work.

Her legions of followers cannot, in large part, be called “fans,” but do include avid viewers, reply guys, bewildered women, judgmental tradwives, hate-watchers, and pop culture fanatics. She collects connoisseurs more than disciples. As such, Althoff is a cipher, and a harbinger of a novel vector of celebrity that’s potentially liberating for women who’ve been trained to seek validation, adoration, and eternal “relevance,” as she puts it. This makes her an intriguingly modern economic actor. When she is recognized in public, she doesn’t tell her children that they just met a few of Mommy’s fans. “I say, these are all Mommy’s coworkers,” she tells me, seeming sincere as she emphasizes that she wouldn’t want her children to think she was traditionally “famous.” But she clearly can’t resist a facetious acknowledgment of how successful her campaign for relevance has been: “They think I have coworkers everywhere.”.

It has been revealed that she “judges relevance by incoming brand deals,” which means she’s willing to maneuver to maintain your attention. “My audience has a lot of men who are just wishing they could see me naked,” she says, a reality she enthusiastically “manipulates a little bit.” She knows her combative approach to flirtation sparks outrage among her male viewers. She’s also aware that many of those men resort to infantile insults, which is where her deadpan self-deprecation comes in: “I want to beat people to the punch,” she claims. “You can't call me ugly and have it hurt me because I called myself ugly first. You can't say I'm not funny: I've already said it.”.

When I relay to Althoff some of the questions my straight male friends had for her, she admits the rabid speculation around her sex life is frustrating but also flattering. “They obviously think I had a chance with these guests,” she deadpans. “There’s no interaction I can have with a man where people aren’t like, Oh, you guys fucked.” Her haters, she’s observed, fall into two camps: Trump voting white men “who think they would never have a chance with me” and believe unmarried mothers to be morally corrupt. On the flip side are “women who are jealous.”.

According to recent reports, her political leanings––which have veered far to the left since her childhood––periodically foment some turmoil among her latest girl squad, but Althoff indicates she also finds much to admire in her conservative cast members lifestyles. “Do I agree with everything in the Church? No. But I see the beauty in the tradwife life.” The relationship between McCall DaPron, a fellow cast member and frenemy turned pseudo sister of Althoff’s, inspired her to break up with her ex, because she saw a healthy dynamic missing from her own relationship. She is committed to maintaining her conviction around political issues her cast members might rather not address: “Does it bother me when I’m the only one in the cast posting about certain things happening in the world? Yes. Fuck ICE, Free Palestine. Free Congo. Free Sudan.”.

Sources indicate that she hopes her onscreen proto-sister wives, and viewers like them, might allow her to “burst that bubble a little bit”—to widen their perspectives, open their eyes, and inspire re-evaluations of concerns close to Althoff’s heart. Admittedly, as the show illuminates, sometimes that means earnestly defending a political position, and other times it means (antifascistly?) refusing to follow the dress code one of the other women attempts to enforce at a party. Observing that male guests on her podcast “always rank themselves a ten out of ten, she notes that “men could be a little more realistic.” She’s not attacking all men, she clarifies, but she would like to alert them to the following: “I don't need to fuck every man that hits on me.”.

She adds, with the sprightly sarcasm that’s become her trademark, one final message to readers of this magazine: “Men who read GQ: be nicer to me. I’m not mean, I don’t hate you, don’t hate me.”.

An All-Time Great Air Jordan Is Returning on Black Friday

📅 21 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (353 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Air Jordan 4 ‘Bred’ is returning.
  • It has been revealed that the ‘Bred’ (short for “black and red”) is one of the original Air Jordan 4 colorways from 1989.
  • Sources indicate that unsurprisingly, Jordan Brand has brought it back a few times over the past few years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sit still for a second. The birds are singing. The sun is shining. The Air Jordan 4 ‘Bred’ is returning. Nature is healing. Everything, for once, is exactly where it should be.

It has been revealed that the ‘Bred’ (short for “black and red”) is one of the original Air Jordan 4 colorways from 1989. Created by legendary Nike designer Tinker Hatfield, it came in slick black nubuck with hits of gray and red throughout. Michael Jordan famously wore a pair when he hit The Shot over Craig Ehlo to knock the Cleveland Cavaliers out of the 1989 NBA Playoffs—so, yeah, there’s a bit of lore there too.

Sources indicate that unsurprisingly, Jordan Brand has brought it back a few times over the past few years. There was a retro in 1999, followed by versions in 2008 and 2012, and then another in 2019, which finally brought the OG “Nike Air” branding back to the heel. Then, in 2024, we got the ‘Bred Reimagined,’ which swapped the classic nubuck for leather. The less said about that one, the better.

In a recent development, because two years later, Jordan Brand is going back to the good stuff. The ‘Bred’ is decked out in black nubuck again, with gray eyelets, red accents around the sole, and the all-notable “Nike Air” stamped across the back. Even the Nike branding on the outsole is returning. Basically, if you looked at the ‘Bred Reimagined’ and thought, “Look how they massacred my boy,” congrats: this one's for you.

And there’s something quite nice about that. The AJ4 has been messed with, remixed, collabed on, and reworked in just about every way possible over the last few years. Some of those experiments have been great! Some… not so much. The ‘Bred’ doesn’t really need any of that. It’s been one of the best Air Jordans on the planet for 37 years. If it ain’t broke, don’t fix it.

The Air Jordan 4 ‘Bred’ is set to drop on November 27 via Nike, the SNKRS app, and select stockists globally.

This story originally appeared on British GQ.

#159035. The 7 Most Common Mistakes Home Cooks Make When Cooking Mashed Potatoes

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (624 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Delish ↗ Open Full Page

The 7 Most Common Mistakes Home Cooks Make When Cooking Mashed Potatoes

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (624 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Delish

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a traditional Thanksgiving meal, mashed potatoes are a seemingly simple side dish that does a lot of heavy lifting.
  • Recent findings suggest that mashed potatoes prove you can transform even the humblest ingredients into something magical.
  • Thankfully, those mistakes are 100% avoidable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a traditional Thanksgiving meal, mashed potatoes are a seemingly simple side dish that does a lot of heavy lifting. They're the perfect vessel for a puddle of gravy, and they’re a creamy complement to everything else on your plate—yes, even your aunt's questionable green bean casserole.

Recent findings suggest that mashed potatoes prove you can transform even the humblest ingredients into something magical. And yet, we've all somehow still eaten bad ones. With a recipe this basic, even the smallest mistakes have nowhere to hide.

Thankfully, those mistakes are 100% avoidable. We rounded up the most common ways to mess up mashed potatoes so that yours turn out as delicious as possible this holiday season.

It has been revealed that it doesn’t matter if you cut your potatoes into a fine dice or rough chunks. Whatever size you pick, stick with it. Making sure your potato pieces are roughly the same size will help them all cook at the same rate. If your knife work is haphazard, you may end up with some pieces that are perfectly cooked, others that are waterlogged and mushy, and some that are still firm in the center.

According to recent reports, like pasta, potatoes need a good amount of seasoning to really shine—which is why salting the cooking water is so vital. You can be generous with the salt, since much of it stays in the water and ends up going down the drain. When you start seasoning early in the cooking process, it’s easier to build flavor and adjust as you go.

It has been revealed that in the hustle of cooking all of your Thanksgiving dishes, you may be tempted to boil your potatoes ahead of time and mash them later in the day. But it’s always better to work with potatoes while they’re still hot and easier to mash. Waiting until they’re cool will likely require far more elbow grease—and you’ll still end up with uneven chunks.

A smooth, creamy mash is the height of decadence. To make sure the potatoes are lump-free, some people may reach for a blender—but this is one of the most consequential mistakes you can make. Potatoes are naturally starchy, and the more you work them, the more starch gets released from their cell walls. Breaking out the blender may be well-intentioned, but it can leave you with potatoes that are gummy and gluey. Instead, opt for the right tool, like a hand masher, food mill, or potato ricer.

It has been revealed that another crucial thing to consider is that potato starches continue absorbing moisture as mashed potatoes sit. They can soak up the milk you’ve added, leaving your potatoes dry and dense. Don’t be afraid to add more liquid—or at least keep some extra on hand to loosen up your mash before serving.

In a recent development, anthony Bourdain famously pointed to generous amounts of salt and butter as part of what makes restaurant food taste so good. That’s especially true for mashed potatoes. You may be scared to add more than a light sprinkle of salt, but don’t forget to taste and adjust the seasoning before serving. A little extra salt can make all the difference for your Thanksgiving dinner.

Industry observers note that whether you’re feeding your immediate family or a small army, you should always make a substantial batch of mashed potatoes. This side is one of the most popular components of a Thanksgiving menu, so it never hurts to make extra. It’s also one of the most versatile dishes for repurposing leftovers. You can transform them into gnocchi, shepherd’s pie, or crispy fried croquettes. It may require more mashing in the moment, but your future self will thank you.

Maple Bourbon Chicken With Brussels Sprouts

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that whisk one 1½" piece ginger, peeled, finely grated, 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, ⅓ cup bourbon, ⅓ cup pure maple syrup, ¼ cup apple cider vinegar, ¼ tsp.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that if you, like most people, hear the term “bourbon chicken” and have no idea what it is, let me call it by its more common name: toothpick chicken. Yes, the suspiciously delicious chicken shelled out at mall food courts on toothpicks is most likely bourbon chicken. Popular at American Chinese or Cajun-style Chinese restaurants, the sticky-sweet chicken is the utter definition of delicious, luring weary shoppers into food courts to find refuge from the bubblegum pink sweatpants and ripped denim. This version takes cues from the classic but swaps in some autumnal ingredients to make it fit for the season. Charred brussels sprouts leaves and pecans add bulk, while maple syrup and apple cider vinegar give it that delightful tart-sweet flavor we know and love. Serve it over rice or noodles or all by its lonesome for a hearty dinner that will take you back to the '90s.

More chicken dinner winners here: Sheet-Pan Hot Honey Chicken and Peaches; Basil Chicken Stir-Fry; and Ginger-Garlic Chicken and Vegetable Stir-Fry.

Industry observers note that whisk one 1½" piece ginger, peeled, finely grated, 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, ⅓ cup bourbon, ⅓ cup pure maple syrup, ¼ cup apple cider vinegar, ¼ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes, 1 Tbsp. cornstarch, ¼ cup low-sodium soy sauce, and ½ cup water in a small bowl to combine. Set sauce aside.

Sources indicate that toss 1½ lb. skinless, boneless chicken breasts, halved crosswise, thinly sliced against the grain, remaining 1 Tbsp. cornstarch, and remaining 1 Tbsp. low-sodium soy sauce in a medium bowl until chicken is coated; set aside.

According to recent reports, heat 2 Tbsp. vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add 1 lb. brussels sprouts, halved through stems, leaves separated, and cook, stirring very occasionally, until just tender and blackened in spots, about 5 minutes. Transfer to another medium bowl.

Recent findings suggest that add more oil if pan looks dry and, working in batches if needed, arrange reserved chicken in a single layer and cook, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through, about 5 minutes. Transfer to bowl with brussels sprouts.

Add reserved sauce to same pan and bring to a simmer. Cook, stirring constantly, until thickened, about 1 minute. Remove pan from heat and return brussels sprouts and chicken to pan; top with 1 cup salted roasted pecans, coarsely chopped. Toss to coat in sauce. Serve chicken and brussels sprouts with steamed white rice if desired.
